title: Interfaces, Linux datapaths and physical-to-virtual infrastructure

paras: An annotated continuation of B011: from ISP optical termination and campus network topology to Linux routing, packet filtering, network namespaces, virtual NICs and infrastructure abstractions.

Source integrity: each handwritten scan referenced below is not yet published here. Technical interpretations and corrections are separately labeled. This is a careful topic-level reading, not a certified word-for-word transcription.

blocks.h2: 01 · Common interfaces and the end-to-end network diagram
paras: From the page: loopback; physical wired Ethernet; wireless interface; network bridge; virtual Ethernet; tunnel/VPN; device identity (MAC, serial); network identity (IP, VLAN, SSID, routing). The illustrated path is ISP backbone → ISP-side OLT → modem/ONT → edge router → firewall cluster → core switches → distribution switch → access switches → Wi-Fi APs / NICs / industrial gateway → IDS/IPS/HSM → ADC .

Clarifications: an OLT is the provider-side termination in a passive optical network; an ONT/ONU is typically the customer-side fiber termination, often integrated with a home gateway. “Modem” is a generic label and does not describe every fiber termination accurately. A firewall cluster is one deployment choice, not a mandatory stage. IDS/IPS and HSM are not normally chained as equivalent inline hops: IDS may monitor mirrored traffic, IPS can be inline, and HSM supplies cryptographic key operations. ADC/load balancing is commonly deployed in front of selected applications, not universally after every endpoint.

Identity layers: MAC addresses identify interfaces within a link-layer domain (and may be virtualized); IP addresses are Layer-3 locators; VLAN tags partition Layer-2 broadcast domains; SSIDs identify wireless networks; routes determine forwarding next hops. Serial numbers are inventory identifiers, not packet forwarding addresses.

blocks.h2: 02 · Linux implementation: routing, firewall, switching and endpoints
paras: From the page: edge router → iptables/nftables and ip route ; eth0 / eth1 as WAN/LAN interfaces; firewall → Netfilter and iptables/firewalld/nftables; switches → Linux bridge and ip link ; NIC/HBA → TUN/TAP and veth pairs; load balancers → HAProxy and NGINX.

Correction: ip route manipulates kernel routing tables. iptables and nft configure packet-filtering/NAT rules via kernel facilities; they are not themselves routing tables. firewalld is a management layer over firewall backends. eth0 and eth1 are interface names, not intrinsically WAN or LAN. Current Linux often uses predictable names such as enp3s0 .

Bridges: Linux bridge forwards Layer-2 frames among attached ports; ip link manages interface state and link configuration, while the bridge utilities or bridge command manage bridge forwarding details. A veth pair behaves like two connected virtual Ethernet ports and is common between a container namespace and host bridge. TUN exposes Layer-3 packets; TAP exposes Layer-2 frames. VPN is a use case for TUN, not a synonym for it.

Useful commands: ip -br link , ip -br addr , ip route show , ip rule show , bridge link , bridge vlan show , sudo nft list ruleset , ip netns list , ss -tulpn . Some commands require privileges and installed tooling.

blocks.h2: 03 · Electronic devices, physical media and virtual equivalents
paras: From the page: physical devices include routers, switches, firewalls, access points, modems, NICs, load balancers, IDS/IPS, repeaters and encoders. Physical media include CAT Ethernet cable, fiber/DSL, RF spectrum, PCIe, and transceivers. Virtual equivalents include VLANs, VPN tunnels, VXLAN, GRE, virtual NICs, VIPs, iSCSI and FCoE.

Key distinction: a physical port is a hardware connector/interface; a virtual interface is a software-managed networking endpoint. A physical cable is a transmission medium, whereas a virtual link is a logical connectivity relationship implemented over underlying physical media. A packet or frame is a protocol data unit, not a direct virtual replacement for an analog/electrical/optical signal. A physical network can host multiple logical networks using VLAN, VRF and overlay encapsulation.

Multiplexing: a single Ethernet trunk can carry multiple VLANs; an IP underlay can carry multiple VXLAN VNIs; a physical NIC can expose multiple virtual functions using SR-IOV. None of these removes dependence on the physical bandwidth, optics, switches and failure domains beneath.

blocks.h2: 04 · Physical device → virtual resource: seven mappings
paras: Original second mapping: device→virtual resource, port→interface, cable→link, path→route, plug→attachment, signal→packet/frame, physical network→logical network. These are design analogies , not one-to-one replacements.

blocks.h2: 05 · Follow one request from the wire into a workload
paras: ISP transport, OLT/ONT where PON is used
WAN interface, routing, NAT as needed
Firewall policy, optional inline IPS
Core/distribution/access switches; VLAN trunks
Physical NIC → bridge/OVS → veth/tap
Pod/VM IP → service or proxy → application socket

What changes at each boundary? Ethernet frames may be re-encapsulated at each routed hop; Layer-3 destinations usually persist end-to-end unless translated by NAT or proxies; VLAN tags are local to participating Layer-2 segments; VXLAN encapsulates tenant frames over an IP underlay. A TCP connection ends at a proxy if the proxy terminates it and creates a separate upstream connection.

tables.h2: 04 · Physical device → virtual resource: seven mappings
rows: A node may itself be a VM or bare-metal server; these are different abstraction levels.
vNIC, veth, tap, virtio-net, SR-IOV VF
Interface names such as eth0/ens160 can name physical or virtual devices.
Linux bridge, Open vSwitch, virtual switch
A bridge/switch forwards L2 traffic; it is not the same as an IP route.
Virtual router, routing table, network namespace
A route table is one component of routing, not a complete router.
Statefulness, enforcement point and provider behavior differ.
VIP, service endpoint, proxy or cloud LB
A VIP alone does not perform load balancing.
PVC is a claim for storage; it is not itself the storage medium.
